chief_complaint: Management of cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes) and knee osteoarthritis pain
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 60-year-old male with a long-standing history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2000, obesity noted since 2007, and prediabetes identified in 2014. Anemia was also first recorded in 2014. He has chronic knee osteoarthritis dating back to 2005, for which he uses naproxen. Current antihypertensive therapy includes lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide, achieving a blood pressure of 132/89 mmHg (stage 1). He reports no recent changes in weight or glucose control; the most recent A1c is 5.9%. He continues to work full‑time and has completed higher education, but his housing situation remains unsatisfactory, potentially affecting adherence and lifestyle. He has had one emergency and one inpatient encounter since 2021, but the majority of his 20 visits are wellness visits, indicating regular engagement with primary care. Diphenhydramine is being taken without a documented indication, suggesting possible insomnia or allergic symptoms.
past_medical_history: Prior appendectomy (1997). Resolved dental issues including gingivitis and primary dental caries (2019-2020). Resolved wrist sprain (2018). History of reported environmental violence (resolved 2019). Previously part-time employed and not in labor force (resolved 2020). Earlier medication review due entries (resolved 2016-2019).
social_determinants: Housing unsatisfactory; full-time employment; higher education; male, 60 years old; white, non-Hispanic; resides in Framingham, MA.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 1 hypertension (132/89), obesity, prediabetes (A1c 5.9%), age 60, male sex, HR 97 bpm. Renal risk: hypertension + NSAID use; eGFR not available. Metabolic risk: obesity and impaired glucose tolerance. Musculoskeletal risk: knee osteoarthritis with NSAID analgesia. Hematologic risk: chronic anemia of unclear etiology. Social risk: unsatisfactory housing may affect adherence and lifestyle. Charlson comorbidity index 1; clinical complexity moderate; polypharmacy low (4 meds).

clinical_impression: The patient is a middle‑aged male with multiple interrelated cardiometabolic risk factors—hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes—managed with antihypertensives but still at stage 1 blood pressure. Chronic knee osteoarthritis contributes to functional limitation and necessitates NSAID use, which raises renal and blood‑pressure concerns. Anemia of unknown cause warrants further work‑up. Social stress from inadequate housing may impede optimal lifestyle modification. Missing key laboratory data (lipids, renal function) limits full risk stratification and therapeutic decision‑making.
